title: calendula incana subsp. algarbiensis
intro: Calendula incana subsp. algarbiensis, commonly known as a type of marigold, is a plant species belonging to the daisy family (Asteraceae). This plant is valued for its potential health benefits, which include anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties, making it useful for wound healing, skin issues, and gastrointestinal problems. The therapeutic actions of Calendula incana subsp. algarbiensis include soothing and calming effects, which can be attributed to its bioactive constituents, such as flavonoids, carotenoids, and phenolic acids. The bioactive constituents of this plant may contribute to its antioxidant, antiseptic, and anti-inflammatory properties, supporting its traditional use in folk medicine.
